transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-01-07
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Sarah Kim (VeraHealth Head of ML), Tom Baker (VeraHealth Platform Eng), Jenna Ortiz (VeraHealth SRE), Mark Liu (VeraHealth CTO)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Diego and Priya from Redwood, and from VeraHealth Sarah, Tom, Jenna and Mark, correct?
[00:12] Sarah Kim: Yep, all here. Thanks Maya.
[00:15] Diego Alvarez: Morning all. I'll jump straight into the benchmark slides but want to call out a couple of caveats up front: our env used the v2 quant profile plus prefix caching enabled, and the baseline provider runs were provided by Vera on their mCPU/gPU mix so not apples-to-apples for exact infra.
[00:30] Tom Baker: Understood - we tried to match as best as possible. We provided the baseline logs last week.
[00:40] Diego Alvarez: Great. Slide 1 - summary table. Median latency on Redwood for the 512-token avg request set was 62ms with 95th at 280ms; baseline provider showed median 85ms and 95th at 430ms. Throughput sustained at 380 rps on a 4-GPU dedicated pool equivalent; baseline averaged around 260 rps.
[01:05] Jenna Ortiz: Those 95th numbers are interesting - what's your measurement for tail-latency? Is that service-side only or includes network RTT?
[01:15] Diego Alvarez: Good call. These numbers are server-side, measured post-model but pre-network egress; we added a client-side RTT estimate separately. In our end-to-end runs we saw 95th at approx 340ms including a 40-60ms typical RTT.
[01:30] Sarah Kim: Ok so end-to-end is what our app will see. The baseline we gave includes their gateway overhead so might be a little inflated.
[01:38] Maya Chen: Quick reminder: the v2 quant profile trades a bit of raw quality for lower cost/latency; Diego, did you run the unconstrained float baseline for quality check?
[01:48] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we ran a float FP16 pass on a subset of prompts. Quality delta was minor for our eval metrics - rouge/emd-style scoring, and human spot checks didn't flag regression for the canned prompts you shared. There were a few corner cases with long context where hallucination risk increased slightly.
[02:10] Mark Liu: For our workflows we have lots of long context threads - around 2k tokens on avg for some features. How does your kernel selection behave there?
[02:22] Diego Alvarez: For >1k sequences we switch kernel paths and the model will prefer larger KV-batch handling. That increases GPU memory but latency per token remains competitive; the quant profile has slightly different timings there, so we suggested a mixed strategy: FP16 for long context routes, v2-quant for short chat responses.
[02:45] Tom Baker: Any empirical numbers for the 2k token load?
[02:50] Diego Alvarez: We did an isolated test: median per-token latency increased ~12%, end-to-end 95th moved from 340ms to around 520ms on the same infra. Baseline provider showed 700ms 95th in their long-context logs, so still an improvement.
[03:10] Jenna Ortiz: We're particularly worried about outliers - our SLA needs 500ms 95th. That 520ms is borderline.
[03:20] Diego Alvarez: Agreed, that's why we want to run the 1k-request tail-latency test over 24-48 hours - tail events often correlate with specific request mixes and cache miss patterns.
[03:30] Sarah Kim: Can you clarify cache miss patterns? We saw KV cache being reported as sometimes not re-used due to prompt variance.
[03:38] Diego Alvarez: Right, prefix/KV caching helps a lot but only when prompts share prefixes. For your dataset we saw about 28% cache-hit rate on average; improving prompt normalization could boost hit rate to 45-50% with big tail improvements.
[03:55] Maya Chen: We can help with a pre-processing suggestion doc. Priya will follow up.
[04:00] Priya Nair: I'll put together a short guide on prompt normalization and a recommended batching configuration with examples.
[04:10] Mark Liu: On the cost side, the pricing numbers in the deck looked promising but we need committed capacity options spelled out.
[04:18] Maya Chen: Sure - I will share the Dedicated capacity tier sheets and committed discounts. We'll include burst policies you can enable.
[04:25] Tom Baker: One question: how did you set batching windows in the test? Our concern is latency unpredictability if you batch too long.
[04:34] Diego Alvarez: We used a 10ms batching window with dynamic batch sizing up to 64 tokens per batch for short chat. For tail-sensitive routes we recommend 0-5ms windows or explicit per-route SLOs which route to a dedicated low-latency pool. That keeps P95 down but costs more.
[04:55] Sarah Kim: That lines up with what our infra folks asked. Any data on jitter for the 10ms window?
[05:02] Diego Alvarez: Jitter median was low; 95th accounted for some batching wait time when request bursts coincide. The 24-hour run will show the real pattern.
[05:12] Jenna Ortiz: SOC2 and KMS integration - we need to validate before a pilot. What's the status?
[05:18] Priya Nair: We have SOC2 Type II docs ready; KMS integrations support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault today, HSM support via partner is available. I'll email the artefacts after the call.
[05:30] Mark Liu: Good. Also curious about private deployment latency differences vs hosted. Are the numbers here from hosted Redwood or Dedicated sim?
[05:40] Diego Alvarez: These were run on a Dedicated-equivalent pool in our hosted infra not on-customer-prem. Private on-prem tends to be similar if you provide identical GPU types and network setup; most differences come from network egress and how you provision shared resources.
[05:55] Sarah Kim: For compliance reasons we may go Private later. We should see near-identical perf if we provision N+1 GPUs similar to your Dedicated.
[06:04] Maya Chen: Agree - we'll help with reference architecture for Private.
[06:10] Diego Alvarez: Back to the benchmarks - we also measured token-efficiency; Redwood produced ~12% fewer inference tokens for same prompts after output normalization, meaning cost-per-response materially lower in practice.
[06:25] Tom Baker: Is that from model tuning or post-processing?
[06:29] Diego Alvarez: Mostly decoding defaults and stop-sequence tuning. Also quant profiles slightly change tokenization edge-cases; we control that in the runtime.
[06:40] Sarah Kim: Any concerns about quality drift over time with quantization? We don't want to see regressions after rolling updates.
[06:47] Diego Alvarez: We run eval sets and quality gates in the rollout pipelines. Canary deploys and automatic rollback on metric regression are part of the platform. We'll attach the eval harness we used.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Quick note: we included a small A/B run in our tests - 10k requests with 50/50 split between v2-quant and FP16. Human raters preferred FP16 in 6/100 cases but the overall metric delta was within your tolerances.
[07:15] Sarah Kim: Ok that's helpful. For the long-context routes we might pin FP16.
[07:21] Mark Liu: On the bench infra - can you share the raw logs and methodology so our infra team can reproduce?
[07:28] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll share the scripts, container images, and the run config. Expect a link in the follow-up.
[07:35] Tom Baker: We saw some outlier HTTP 502s in your logs - what caused that?
[07:41] Diego Alvarez: Those were transient overloaded worker restarts traced to an edge case in our batch splitter with very large sequences; we've patched it and re-ran a subset. The latest runs in the folder exclude those.
[07:55] Jenna Ortiz: Good to know. We'll need the revision notes for our compliance team.
[08:00] Priya Nair: I'll include a changelog and repro steps.
[08:07] Sarah Kim: What's the plan for the long tail 1k-request run? How long will it take and what are we measuring?
[08:14] Diego Alvarez: We'll run a 24-hour continuous run with 1k concurrent clients that ramp and sustain; measure median/95/99 percentiles, eviction rates for KV cache, batch-size distribution, and GPU utilization. We'll also capture end-to-end RTT with synthetic clients to include network.
[08:32] Maya Chen: Diego, can you commit to sharing preliminary numbers in one week?
[08:36] Diego Alvarez: Yes - preliminary in 7 days, full artifact in 14.
[08:40] Sarah Kim: Perfect.
[08:42] Mark Liu: Also, can you show cost extrapolation for 100M tokens/month with both hosted and Dedicated pricing?
[08:50] Maya Chen: We'll include a cost model spreadsheet with run assumptions; I'll send that in the follow-up.
[08:55] Tom Baker: On the security front - SSO/SAML and RBAC support details?
[09:00] Priya Nair: We support SAML SSO and granular RBAC per route and per model; we can map to your existing roles. Details in the security pack.
[09:08] Jenna Ortiz: Good. Any regulatory notes for PHI handling?
[09:12] Priya Nair: We have controls for data residency and audited logs; Private deployments are recommended for PHI-heavy workloads. We'll flag those in the docs.
[09:22] Sarah Kim: For the final pilot decision, our eval criteria: P95 under 500ms for targeted routes, no material quality regression, clear committed pricing, and SOC2 + KMS proof. Are we aligned?
[09:33] Maya Chen: That's aligned. We'll aim to meet those requirements.
[09:36] Diego Alvarez: One more technical note: you mentioned 2k token threads and hallucination risk - we recommend a small reranker step on candidate outputs for critical workflows; we can demo a lightweight reranker in the next session.
[09:49] Sarah Kim: That would be useful.
[09:51] Mark Liu: Recap and next steps please.
[09:55] Maya Chen: Sure - recap: Diego will run the 24-hour 1k-client tail-latency benchmark and share preliminary numbers by 2026-01-14. Maya will share pricing, Dedicated commitment options, and the cost model by 2026-01-09. Priya will send SOC2 docs, KMS notes, and prompt normalization suggestions by 2026-01-11. Vera will provide anonymized prompt set by 2026-01-12. We'll schedule an architecture review for Private deployments for week of 2026-01-19.
[10:20] Sarah Kim: Thanks, that sounds good.
[10:23] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and links. End call.

Notes/Links referenced: benchmark artifacts link (shared drive), pricing spreadsheet (will be sent), SOC2 pack (to be attached).
